mainTopic: The end of the dispute between אביי and רבא about קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה, and רב's lessons from the משנה of the five women, especially about betrothing with a stolen item.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about two brothers who betrothed two sisters without knowing which was whose. The גמרא adds that חליצה must come before יבום. Then a ברייתא from טביומי, 'one of your daughters is betrothed to one of my sons,' shows that a betrothal which can never lead to living together is still valid. That refutes רבא, and the גמרא rules like אביי in six cases, remembered by the sign יע"ל קג"ם. Next, רב draws lessons from the משנה of the five women. A man may betroth with שביעית fruit, but not with a stolen item, even one stolen from her. A woman can also act as an agent for her future צרה. רב was unsure of a fourth lesson because it depends on the dispute between אביי and רבא. רבי יוחנן is pleased that רב agrees with him that a stolen item is not the robber's. Finally, a ברייתא saying stolen money works for קידושין is explained as being only about a coin grabbed from the woman herself.

steps.title: End of the brothers-and-sisters case: who does חליצה and who may do יבום
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about two brothers who betrothed two sisters (without knowing which was whose) finishes. After the two men die, the lone brother of one does חליצה with both sisters. Of the other man's two brothers, one does חליצה and the other may do יבום. If they married first without asking, we don't force them apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one brother does חליצה with both women. Of the two brothers, one does חליצה and one does יבום. If they went ahead and married on their own, we do not take the women away from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting earlier, about two dead men whose widows are sisters and nobody knows which widow belonged to whom. It now gives the last rules: who does חליצה, who may do יבום, and what happens if they married without asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One dead man left one surviving brother, and the other dead man left two. The lone brother cannot know which sister is his brother's widow, so he does חליצה with both and frees whichever one is tied to him. In the other family, one brother does חליצה and the other may do יבום; the ברייתא adds that if they married first, the marriage stays.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that frees a childless widow from her tie to her dead husband's brother
When the dead husband's brother marries the childless widow
They went ahead and married first, without asking the court
We do not take the women away from them; the marriage stands

phrases.english: the one brother performs חליצה with both of them,
and of the two brothers, one performs חליצה and one performs יבום.
If they went ahead and married them first,
we do not take them out of their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that the גמרא was quoting just before this section began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lone brother does חליצה with both sisters; of the two brothers, one does חליצה and one may do יבום; if they married first, the marriages stand.

steps.title: The order matters: חליצה must come before יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ruling 'we don't take them away' only works if the חליצה happened first and the יבום afterward. If the יבום came first, it doesn't work, because he may have married a woman who was still tied to another family.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is only when they did חליצה first and then יבום. But if they did יבום first and then חליצה, no. That is because he may be marrying a יבמה who is not yet free to marry an outsider.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining the last line of the ברייתא. The marriage only stands if the חליצה was done before the יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until the lone brother has done חליצה with both sisters, each sister might still be tied to his family. If a brother from the other family does יבום before that, he might be marrying someone else's יבמה, who is forbidden to anyone outside that family. Once the חליצה is done first, that worry is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Specifically; only in this case
And then; afterward
Runs into; ends up dealing with
A יבמה who is not yet free to marry an outsider, literally 'a יבמה to the marketplace'

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא lets them marry in any order. The גמרא limits it: the חליצה that frees the woman from the other family must come first.

phrases.english: Specifically when they first perform חליצה and afterward perform יבום,
but if they first perform יבום and afterward חליצה, no,
since he is running into a יבמה who is bound and not free to marry an outsider.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the limits of the last clause of the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A marriage done without asking stands only if the חליצה was done before the יבום; if the יבום came first, it is not allowed.

steps.title: טביומי's ברייתא: five sons, five daughters, and an unclear betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from טביומי. A man with five sons tells a man with five daughters, 'One of your daughters is betrothed to one of my sons.' Each daughter needs five גיטין. If a son dies, each daughter needs four גיטין plus חליצה from one brother. The betrothal counts, even though it could never lead to living together, and that challenges רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what טביומי taught: one man has five sons and another has five daughters. The first says, 'One of your daughters is betrothed to one of my sons.' Each daughter needs five גיטין. If one son dies, each daughter needs four גיטין and חליצה from one of the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to attack רבא's view. רבא holds that a betrothal which can never lead to living together is not a real betrothal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody knows which son is betrothed to which daughter, and every daughter might be the sister of a son's real wife. So no son may ever live with any of the daughters; this is קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה. Still, the ברייתא treats the betrothal as real and requires גיטין and even חליצה, which matches אביי and goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothed
Bills of divorce (plural of גט)
A betrothal where the couple can never be permitted to live together

steps.whyThisMatters: This source shows a betrothal that could never lead to living together, from start to finish, and still treats it as fully real. That is exactly the question אביי and רבא argue about.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as טביומי taught:
This man has five sons
and that man has five daughters,
and the first one said: 'One of your daughters
is betrothed to one of my sons,'

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת צְרִיכָה חֲמִשָּׁה גִּיטִּין.
phrases.english: each and every one of the daughters needs five bills of divorce.
If one of the sons died,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת צְרִיכָה אַרְבָּעָה גִּיטִּין,
phrases.english: each and every one needs four bills of divorce,
and חליצה from one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier ברייתא (steps 1-2) could be explained away. Now the גמרא brings a new source to challenge רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה is not a valid betrothal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No son can ever live with any daughter, since she might be his wife's sister, yet the ברייתא requires גיטין and חליצה. That means the betrothal is real.

steps.title: The usual defense doesn't fit this case
steps.stepSummary: Someone might defend רבא by saying that here too, the couple was first known and only later mixed up. The גמרא rejects this, because the ברייתא's own words, 'one of your daughters to one of my sons,' show it was unclear from the very start.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that here too it means they were first identified and only later got mixed up, that can't be. The ברייתא says 'one of your daughters to one of my sons.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the answer that saved רבא from the earlier ברייתא. It says that answer won't work here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא was defended by saying the betrothal was clear when it happened and only got confused later, so it could lead to living together at the start. Here the words 'one of your daughters to one of my sons' show nobody ever knew who was matched to whom. So the betrothal could never lead to living together, not even for a moment.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say; brings up a possible answer in order to reject it
Here too
They were first identified and later got mixed up
It teaches; points to the exact wording of the source

phrases.english: And if you would say: here too
it is where they were identified and in the end got mixed up,
phrases.notes: This is the answer the גמרא gave earlier to protect רבא from the brothers-and-sisters ברייתא.

phrases.english: but it teaches 'one of your daughters to one of my sons'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכִי נָמֵי כְּשֶׁהוּכְּרוּ וּלְבַסּוֹף נִתְעָרְבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible defense of רבא against the challenge in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the 'identified and later mixed up' answer for טביומי's ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording 'one of your daughters to one of my sons' shows the betrothal was unclear from the very beginning.

steps.title: רבא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבא's view has been fully disproven.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רבא, a real refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that רבא loses this argument. No answer is left for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the 'mixed up later' defense fails, טביומי's ברייתא stands as a clear case of קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה being valid. Saying 'תיובתא' twice means the refutation is final.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; a source disproves an Amora's view and no answer is left

steps.whatToRemember: קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה, a betrothal that could never lead to living together, is still a valid betrothal. אביי is right and רבא is refuted.

phrases.english: The refutation of רבא is a conclusive refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once the defense in step 4 fails, the challenge from step 3 defeats רבא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's view is refuted; a betrothal that cannot lead to living together is valid, like אביי.

steps.title: The six cases where the הלכה follows אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a general rule. Usually the הלכה follows רבא against אביי, but in six cases, remembered by the sign יע"ל קג"ם, the הלכה follows אביי. The case just discussed is one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows אביי in the cases marked יע"ל קג"ם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes with a well-known memory sign listing the six disputes where the הלכה follows אביי rather than רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally when אביי and רבא argue, the הלכה is like רבא. This line lists the six exceptions. The ק in the sign stands for קידושין, the case just settled.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is like him
Memory sign for six cases: יאוש שלא מדעת, עד זומם, לחי, קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה, גילוי דעת בגט, מומר
A memory sign made of letters to help remember a list

steps.whatToRemember: The general rule is that the הלכה follows רבא over אביי, except in the six cases of יע"ל קג"ם.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for deciding הלכה all over the תלמוד, and many סוגיות rely on it.

phrases.english: And the halakha is in accordance with Abaye
in the cases marked yod-ayin-lamed, kuf-gimmel-mem.
phrases.notes: Each letter is a case: יאוש, עד זומם, לחי, קידושין, גט, מומר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא is refuted in step 5, the גמרא places this ruling in the list of six cases where the הלכה follows אביי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the six cases of יע"ל קג"ם, including קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה, the הלכה follows אביי.

steps.title: רב says the משנה teaches four lessons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the משנה about five women. רב says four lessons can be learned from it, but he only firmly held three.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'An incident with five women.' רב said: Four lessons can be learned from this משנה. And רב held three of them firmly in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה of the five women and brings רב's claim that it teaches four lessons. This is a setup line, and the next steps list the lessons one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a man betrothed five women, two of them sisters, with a basket of שביעית figs from their own field. One woman accepted it for all of them, and the sisters were not betrothed. רב says this one story hides four separate rules, but only three were clear to him.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a real event recorded in the משנה
Learn from it, a lesson drawn from a source
Held in his hand, meaning he knew it clearly

phrases.english: An incident with five women.
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of the משנה. Two of the five women were sisters, and he betrothed them all with one basket of figs.

phrases.english: Rav said:
Learn from the mishna four things,
and Rav held three in his hand.
phrases.notes: He means רב was sure of three lessons but not of the fourth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִמַּתְנִיתִין אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the closing rule about אביי and רבא, the גמרא returns to the משנה of the five women to draw out its lessons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה of the five women teaches four lessons, and רב was certain of three.

steps.title: Sabbatical produce works for betrothal, but stolen property does not
steps.stepSummary: Lesson one: betrothal with שביעית produce is valid. Lesson two: betrothal with stolen property is not valid, even if it was stolen from the woman herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it: if a man betroths a woman with שביעית fruit, she is betrothed. And learn from it: if he betroths her with something stolen, she is not betrothed, even if it was stolen from her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב lists his first two lessons from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, שביעית fruit can be used to betroth a woman. Second, stolen property cannot. This holds even if he stole it from her and then handed it back to her as the betrothal; we do not say that taking it means she gave it up to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce of the Sabbatical (seventh) year
Stolen property
She is betrothed

steps.confusionAlert: 'גזל דידה' does not mean she stole something. It means the man stole it from her and then used it to betroth her.

phrases.english: Learn from it:
one who betroths with Sabbatical-year produce – she is betrothed,
and learn from it:
if he betrothed her with a stolen item – she is not betrothed,
even with her own stolen item.
phrases.notes: He means something the man stole from her.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ בְּפֵירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית – מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts listing the lessons promised in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Betrothal with שביעית produce is valid, and betrothal with stolen property is not valid, even if it was stolen from the woman herself.

steps.title: Proving both lessons from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where both lessons come from. The משנה stresses that the figs were theirs and were שביעית, which means the betrothal worked only because שביעית fruit is ownerless.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? Because the משנה says the figs were theirs and were of שביעית. The reason it worked is שביעית, since the fruit is ownerless. But in the other years of the seven-year cycle, it would not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we learn the first two lessons, and then proves them from the משנה's exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the betrothal worked, שביעית fruit must be usable for קידושין. That is lesson one. The משנה needed to add that it was שביעית, so in any other year the figs from their field would count as stolen and the betrothal would fail, even though she was the owner. That is lesson two.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? A request for the source of a claim
Ownerless property that anyone may take
The years of the seven-year cycle

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one extra detail in a משנה can teach a rule by implication: if the detail had been missing, the outcome would have been different.

phrases.english: From where?
From the fact that it teaches:
it was theirs,
and it was of the Sabbatical year –
the reason is that it is Sabbatical, since it is ownerless,
but of the other years of the seven-year cycle – no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? מִדְּקָתָנֵי: שֶׁלָּהֶם הָיְתָה וְשֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the two lessons from step 8 with the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The two lessons: שביעית produce works for קידושין, and stolen property does not, even if it was stolen from her.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's words 'שלהם היתה ושל שביעית היתה', read as an implication.

steps.title: A woman can be an agent for another woman, even as her rival wife
steps.stepSummary: Lesson three: one woman can accept קידושין on behalf of another woman, even though this makes them צרות married to the same man.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: a woman can become an agent for her fellow woman, even in a case where she becomes her rival wife.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives his third lesson, which comes from the fact that one woman accepted the basket for all five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, one woman accepted the betrothal for herself and the others. So she was helping the man marry other women besides her, which would make them her צרות, and still her agency worked. We do not worry that she would not act faithfully for a woman who will be her rival.

keyTerms.meaning: An agent who acts on someone else's behalf
A rival wife, another wife of the same husband

phrases.english: And learn from it:
a woman can become an agent for her fellow,
and even where she becomes her rival wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: אִשָּׁה נַעֲשֵׂית שָׁלִיחַ לַחֲבֶירְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the third lesson to the two in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman can act as an agent to accept קידושין for another woman, even when this makes her the other woman's צרה.

steps.title: What is the fourth lesson?
steps.stepSummary: רב promised four lessons but listed only three, so the גמרא asks what the missing one is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which lesson is the fourth. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said four lessons and gave only three. The גמרא wants to identify the fourth lesson he did not hold firmly.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one, the remaining item

phrases.english: And what is the other one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notices the gap between the four lessons promised and the three listed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the fourth lesson רב said could be learned from the משנה?

steps.title: The fourth lesson is betrothal that cannot lead to living together
steps.stepSummary: The fourth lesson is about קידושין שאין מסורים לביאה, a betrothal that can never lead to married life together.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the rule of a betrothal that is not given over to living together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the fourth lesson is about a betrothal that can never lead to living together, which is the same topic just argued about by אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sisters in the משנה can never both be married to the same man. So betrothing them together is the kind of קידושין that can never lead to living together, and the משנה touches on whether such a betrothal counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothal that can never lead to living together as husband and wife

phrases.english: Betrothal that is not given over to consummation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fourth lesson concerns קידושין שאין מסורים לביאה.

steps.title: Then why didn't רב count it?
steps.stepSummary: If this is a real lesson from the משנה, the גמרא asks why רב did not include it in his list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him count it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב: if the fourth lesson is known, he should have listed it with the other three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we can name the fourth lesson, it seems strange that רב said he only held three. The question pushes the גמרא to explain why he held back.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him count it, a challenge to include something left out

phrases.english: Then let him count it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's statement from step 7, based on the answer in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that he held only three of the four lessons.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the fourth lesson is clearly about קידושין שאין מסורים לביאה, רב should simply have counted it.

steps.title: רב was unsure whether the משנה follows אביי or רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב did not count the fourth lesson because he was unsure whether the משנה should be read like אביי or like רבא, so he could not say what it teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he was uncertain whether it follows אביי or רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב left out the fourth lesson because he did not know which way the משנה teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא disagree about whether a betrothal that can never lead to living together counts, and each reads the משנה his own way. רב knew the משנה deals with this topic but could not tell which reading was right, so he could not state the lesson firmly.

keyTerms.meaning: He was in doubt, he was unsure

steps.whatToRemember: רב finds four lessons in the משנה of the five women. Three are certain: שביעית produce works for קידושין, stolen property does not even if it was stolen from her, and a woman can be an agent for her צרה. The fourth, about קידושין שאין מסורים לביאה, stays unclear because it depends on the dispute between אביי and רבא.

phrases.english: Because he was uncertain
whether it is like Abaye or like Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דִּמְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ אִי כְּאַבָּיֵי אִי כְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why רב held back: the lesson is real, but its content is uncertain.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fourth lesson is clear, so רב should have counted it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב knew the משנה deals with this topic but did not know whether it follows אביי or רבא, so he did not count it as a firm lesson.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן hears רב's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells רבי יוחנן what רב taught, and רבי יוחנן asks, 'Did רב really say that?'
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא moved up to ארץ ישראל, he told this teaching to רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן said to him: Did רב say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story: רב's teaching reached רבי יוחנן in ארץ ישראל, and he asked a surprised question about it. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא tries to figure out what his question means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'Did רב say this?' sound like doubt or disagreement. The next steps test whether רבי יוחנן really disagrees with רב, especially with the idea that one cannot make קידושין with a stolen item.

keyTerms.meaning: When he went up (to ארץ ישראל from בבל)
A teaching or halachic statement
In front of him
Did he say? (a question that can sound like surprise or doubt)

phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira went up
phrases.notes: 'Went up' means he moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he said this teaching
before Rabbi Yochanan.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי אָמַר רַב הָכִי?
phrases.english: He said to him: Did Rav say so?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְלֵיק רַבִּי זֵירָא אַמְרַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the list of רב's lessons to how רבי יוחנן reacted when he heard them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן reacts to רב's teaching with the question 'Did רב say this?'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן holds the same idea himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן could disagree, since he himself rules that a stolen item does not belong to the robber.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't he himself say so? Didn't רבי יוחנן say: If someone robbed an item and the owner has not given up hope of getting it back, neither of them can make it הקדש. The robber can't, because it is not his. The owner can't, because it is not in his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב. It quotes רבי יוחנן's own ruling, which follows the same logic as רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that a robber cannot make a stolen item הקדש, because it still is not his. The same logic means he could not use it for קידושין either. So why would רבי יוחנן be surprised at רב?

keyTerms.meaning: He robbed (took by force)
The owner giving up hope of getting the item back
To give an item to the בית המקדש, making it holy
In his possession or control

phrases.english: But didn't he himself say [so]?!
Didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
If one robbed and the owners did not give up hope,
neither of them can consecrate it,
this one because it is not his,
and that one because it is not in his possession.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the real owner. He still owns it, but he doesn't have it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא לָא אֲמַר?! וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of step 15 as a sign that רבי יוחנן disagreed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי יוחנן's question shows he disagrees with רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן himself rules that a stolen item is not the robber's. That fits רב's view, so he should not object.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was pleased, not objecting
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's question really meant: 'Did רב say the same as me?'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant to say to him: Did רב say like me?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads רבי יוחנן's words. His question was a pleased surprise that רב agreed with him, not a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words, 'Did רב say this?', can mean 'I disagree' or 'How nice, he agrees with me.' The גמרא picks the second meaning, so there is no argument between רב and רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant
Like me, in agreement with my view

phrases.english: This is what he said to him:
Did Rav say in accordance with me?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by rereading רבי יוחנן's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the meaning of a statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was questioning רב's teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן was happily noting that רב agreed with his own view.

steps.title: A ברייתא says קידושין with a stolen item works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from a ברייתא that says a woman is מקודשת even with robbed or stolen money.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this from a ברייתא: If he made קידושין with something robbed, taken by force, or stolen, or he grabbed a סלע from her hand and made קידושין with it, she is מקודשת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to go directly against רב's teaching that one cannot make קידושין with a stolen item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds the stolen item is not the man's, so the קידושין should fail. The ברייתא says the woman is מקודשת, which sounds like stolen items do work for קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking something by force, even if the owner is paid against his will
Stealing in secret
A silver coin
She is betrothed

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If he betrothed her with something robbed, taken by force, or stolen,
or if he grabbed a sela from her hand and betrothed her,
she is betrothed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רב's teaching itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that קידושין with a stolen item does not work.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא openly says that with robbed or stolen items, she is מקודשת.

steps.title: The ברייתא means an item stolen from her
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about an item the man stole from the woman herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about an item that was stolen from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is not about an item stolen from some other person. It is about something taken from the woman herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the item was hers and she accepts it as קידושין, that can show she is letting him keep it, so the קידושין works. Read this way, the ברייתא is not about property stolen from other people.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that ברייתא
Hers

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean stolen items usually work for קידושין. The answer only limits the ברייתא to an item taken from the woman herself. In step 8 רב said that in the משנה's case even her own stolen item did not work.

phrases.english: There it is with her own stolen item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about items stolen from anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about an item stolen from the woman herself.

steps.title: The last case already covers her own item
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists 'he grabbed a סלע from her' separately, which suggests the first case is about items stolen from other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last part of the ברייתא teaches 'or he grabbed a סלע of hers,' that shows the first part is talking about items stolen from anyone else!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 19. The ברייתא has a separate case about the woman's own coin, so the first case must be about something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first case were already about her own item, why add a second case about grabbing her coin? Adding it suggests the first case is about items stolen from other people, which goes against רב again.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a teaching
The first part of a teaching
This shows, by implication
Of the world, meaning belonging to anyone else

phrases.english: But since the last clause teaches:
or he grabbed a sela of hers,
this shows that in the first clause
we are dealing with an item stolen from others!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 19 using the structure of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the first part of the ברייתא is about the woman's own item.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A separate last case about her own coin means the first case must be about other people's property.

steps.title: The last case only explains the first
steps.stepSummary: The last part of the ברייתא is not a new case. It shows how the first case happens: he grabbed her own coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is explaining itself. 'He made קידושין with something robbed, taken by force, or stolen.' How does that happen? For example, he grabbed a סלע from her hand and made קידושין with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא has one case, not two. The words about grabbing her coin are an example of the first part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read the 'or' as 'how so? for example.' Then the whole ברייתא is about the woman's own item. Nothing in it goes against רב's rule about items stolen from other people.

keyTerms.meaning: It is explaining (the earlier words)
How so?
For example

steps.whatToRemember: רב and רבי יוחנן agree that a stolen item is not the robber's to use, so a man cannot make קידושין with it. The ברייתא that says she is מקודשת is read as being only about a coin he grabbed from the woman herself, not about property stolen from others.

phrases.english: It is explaining:
phrases.notes: The ברייתא isn't adding a second case. It is showing how the first case happens.

phrases.english: He betrothed her with something robbed, taken by force, or stolen. How so?
For example, he grabbed a sela from her hand
and betrothed her with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by rereading how the ברייתא is built.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the structure of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists two separate cases: items stolen from others, and her own coin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second clause only explains the first, so the whole ברייתא is about her own item.
